bodies.build-bins:
name: build bins (pohunekd + pohunek-sessiond + pohunek)
    needs: [test-selection, reuse]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.test-selection.result != 'success' || needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed != 'true' || needs.test-selection.outputs.mode != 'none' || needs.test-selection.outputs.docs_only != 'true') && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'build-bins') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 # glibc floor of the shipped binaries (#1731)
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        id: infra-1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install mold linker
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-mold
        timeout-minutes: 10
        with:
          version: ${{ env.MOLD_VERSION }}
          sha256: ${{ env.MOLD_SHA256 }}

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          # Designated `bins` saver; the upgrade workflow restores it. Both
          # run on ubuntu-24.04, the glibc floor of the shipped binaries.
          shared-key: bins
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # The real daemon spawns `pohunek-sessiond` by path, and the Hermes plugin
      # e2e drives the real `pohunek` CLI, so all three binaries are needed.
      - name: Build daemon, session worker, and CLI
        run: cargo build --locked -p pohunek-daemon -p pohunek-session-worker -p pohunek-cli

      - name: Upload built binaries
        id: infra-2
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pohunek-bins
          path: |
            target/debug/pohunekd
            target/debug/pohunek-sessiond
            target/debug/pohunek
          if-no-files-found: error

      # The daemon serves `hermes` only from the official Hermes package, so the
      # Hermes plugin e2e installs the archive built from runtime-packages/hermes
      # through a throwaway signed catalog whose trust anchor it places beside
      # its own copy of the daemon. The SDK job has no Rust toolchain, so both
      # are built here.
      - name: Build the Hermes package and its throwaway catalog
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rm -rf target/hermes-e2e
          mkdir -p target/hermes-e2e
          scripts/build-hermes-package target/hermes-e2e/hermes.tar.zst
          cargo xtask hermes throwaway-catalog \
            --package target/hermes-e2e/hermes.tar.zst \
            --output-dir target/hermes-e2e/catalog

      - name: Upload the Hermes package and its throwaway catalog
        id: infra-3
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: hermes-e2e-package
          path: target/hermes-e2e
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Cancel the run (fail fast)
        if: failure() && env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE == '' && steps.infra-1.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-2.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-3.outcome != 'failure' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        uses: ./.github/actions/cancel-run
      - name: Note the infrastructure failure (no cancel)
        if: failure() && (env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE != '' || steps.infra-1.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-2.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-3.outcome == 'failure')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::notice title=Infrastructure failure::tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step); check the step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too; not cancelling, rerun this job alone"

  # Skipped on the docs-only path of a pull request (#1218): a narrowed

name: build tests (nextest archive)
    needs: reuse
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'build-tests') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    env:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        id: infra-1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install mold linker
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-mold
        timeout-minutes: 10
        with:
          version: ${{ env.MOLD_VERSION }}
          sha256: ${{ env.MOLD_SHA256 }}

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: test-debug
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@4cef1412cce204788f482e778a0b9187f9626a29 # v2.87.21
        id: infra-2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      # The archive holds the test binaries, the runnable bins the tests spawn,
      # and pohunek-sessiond (archive.include in .config/nextest.toml, an error

          size="$(stat -c %s "$RUNNER_TEMP/nextest-archive.tar.zst")"
          echo "nextest archive: ${size} bytes" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The archive is already zstd-compressed: store it as is (level 0).
      - name: Upload test archive

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: nextest-archive
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nextest-archive.tar.zst
          retention-days: 1
          compression-level: 0
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Cancel the run (fail fast)
        if: failure() && env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE == '' && steps.infra-1.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-2.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-3.outcome != 'failure' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        uses: ./.github/actions/cancel-run
      - name: Note the infrastructure failure (no cancel)
        if: failure() && (env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE != '' || steps.infra-1.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-2.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-3.outcome == 'failure')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::notice title=Infrastructure failure::tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step); check the step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too; not cancelling, rerun this job alone"

  # Full release build: schedule, push to main, manual dispatch, or a pull
  # request that changes a `release` filter input.
bodies.fast-tests:
name: tests (${{ matrix.shard }}, fast)
    needs: [build-tests, test-selection, reuse]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-tests.result == 'success' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.test-selection.result != 'success' || needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed != 'true' || needs.test-selection.outputs.fast_shards != '[]') && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'fast-tests') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The shards a narrowed selection plans; every shard otherwise.
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true' && needs.test-selection.outputs.fast_shards || '["core", "daemon", "cli"]') }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: relocated
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        id: infra-1
        with:
          path: relocated
          persist-credentials: false

      # The sparse test tree and the relocated checkout hold no .github/actions
      # at the workspace root when the cancel step runs, so the action is copied
      # out of the checkout next to it.
      - name: Keep the fail-fast action
        run: cp -R .github/actions/cancel-run "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/cancel-run-action"

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@4cef1412cce204788f482e778a0b9187f9626a29 # v2.87.21
        id: infra-2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      - name: Download test archive
        id: infra-3
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: nextest-archive
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nextest-archive

      - name: Download test selection
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true'
        id: infra-4
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-selection
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/test-selection

      # A test that runs cargo, such as `cargo metadata` in xtask's affected
      # tests, finds the pinned toolchain installed. Otherwise rustup installs
      # it mid-test, and concurrent installs race on ~/.rustup/downloads.
      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./relocated/.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Check script regressions
        if: matrix.shard == 'core' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.test-selection.result != 'success' || needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed != 'true' || needs.test-selection.outputs.script_tests != 'false')
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'

      # Every workflow installs Rust from rust-toolchain.toml or a dated nightly.
      - name: Check the Rust toolchain pin
        if: matrix.shard == 'core'
        run: scripts/check-rust-toolchain-pin

      # The tests run from a tree holding only the files whose change selects
      # them, so a read of any other path fails instead of passing with the
      # test skipped. A run without sparse.txt keeps the full tree.
      - name: Keep only the selection's files in the tree
        if: env.TEST_SELECTION_SPARSE == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sparse="$RUNNER_TEMP/test-selection/sparse.txt"
          if [ -f "$sparse" ]; then
            git sparse-checkout set --no-cone --stdin < "$sparse"
            echo "sparse tree of $(wc -l < "$sparse") files"
          fi

      # No dependency on Clippy, PostgreSQL, PTYs, or the release build.
      - name: Run fast shard
        shell: bash
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          NARROWED: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          selection=()
          if [ "$NARROWED" = true ]; then
            selection=(--selection "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-selection/selection.json")
          fi
          python3 scripts/test-partitions --archive-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/nextest-archive/nextest-archive.tar.zst" run "$SHARD" "${selection[@]}"

      - name: Summarize flaky tests
        if: always()
        run: python3 scripts/junit-flaky-summary --label "fast ${{ matrix.shard }}" target/nextest/ci/junit.xml

      - name: Upload shard timing report
        if: always()
        id: infra-5
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: nextest-junit-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: relocated/target/nextest/ci/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn
      - name: Cancel the run (fail fast)
        if: failure() && env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE == '' && steps.infra-1.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-2.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-3.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-4.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-5.outcome != 'failure' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        uses: ./cancel-run-action
      - name: Note the infrastructure failure (no cancel)
        if: failure() && (env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE != '' || steps.infra-1.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-2.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-3.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-4.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-5.outcome == 'failure')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::notice title=Infrastructure failure::tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step); check the step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too; not cancelling, rerun this job alone"

    # Determine which CI jobs the changed files require. Heavy non-default jobs
  # (feature-powerset, macOS contracts, Hermes compatibility, and TS-binding
  # drift) only run when their inputs change or on a schedule; the
  # always-critical jobs (fmt, clippy, fast tests, heavy tests, doctests,
  # docs check) still run on every push and PR. The release build
  # is gated by the `release` filter. Every
  # filter lists rust-toolchain.toml and .github/actions/setup-rust/**, so a
  # toolchain pin change runs every Rust job.
bodies.feature-matrix:
name: cargo-hack (feature powerset)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 # not yet run on ubuntu-26.04 (#1731)
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Expensive (issue #125): run only on schedule, push to main, manual
    # dispatch (always a full run), or when the dependency graph / feature
    # set / CI workflow changes.
    needs: [changes, reuse]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || needs.changes.outputs.feature_matrix == 'true') && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'feature-matrix') }}
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install mold linker
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-mold
        timeout-minutes: 10
        with:
          version: ${{ env.MOLD_VERSION }}
          sha256: ${{ env.MOLD_SHA256 }}

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust
        with:
          components: clippy

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: hack
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Install cargo-hack
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@4cef1412cce204788f482e778a0b9187f9626a29 # v2.87.21
        with:
          tool: cargo-hack

      # Validates every feature combination compiles. knowledge gates its
      # protocol bridge behind the `protocol` feature; --all-features only
      # exercises the everything-on case.
      - name: Check feature powerset
        run: cargo hack --feature-powerset --workspace clippy --all-targets

  # Pull requests get the stable source-level `shear` job below. cargo-udeps
  # needs the nightly toolchain and a full workspace build, so it runs only on
  # push to main, the nightly sweep, and manual dispatch. It is the backstop for
  # what cargo-shear cannot see: a dependency whose only reference sits in code
  # compiled out for the host (e.g. `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` on Linux).
bodies.hermes-compatibility-macos:
name: pinned Hermes compatibility (macOS arm64, model-free)
    # A pull request runs it only for its narrow input filter (issue #1050);
    # core inputs are covered by the main and nightly tiers. The Linux
    # `hermes-package` job follows the runtime package selection instead.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.result == 'success' && needs.macos-release-build.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'push' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && (inputs.tier == 'main' || inputs.tier == 'nightly')) || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.hermes_macos == 'true')) && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'hermes-compatibility-macos') }}
    needs: [changes, macos-release-build, reuse]
    runs-on: macos-15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    env:
      MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "14.0"
      # mold is Linux-only: keep the default linker on macOS runners.
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    # The debug build of the CLI integration tests for the real Hermes session
    # takes a large share of a cold run; the release daemon comes from
    # `macos-release-build`.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        id: infra-1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Verify native runner architecture
        shell: bash
        run: test "$(uname -m)" = "arm64"

      # Bootstrap python3 for the provisioner's helper programs and the shell
      # tests. setup-python installs the python.org framework build here, whose
      # bin/python3.x re-executes Python.app; the Hermes venv therefore runs
      # the provisioner's pinned non-framework standalone CPython instead.
      - name: Install Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-uv
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      # The runtime is provisioned by scripts/provision-hermes-compat, which
      # needs curl, git, pkill, python3, tar, uv, and one SHA-256 tool (macOS
      # ships shasum).
      - name: Require provisioning prerequisites
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for executable in curl git pkill python3 tar uv shasum; do
            command -v "$executable" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
              || { echo "required executable is unavailable: $executable" >&2; exit 1; }
          done
          /bin/bash --version | head -n 1

      # Same inputs as the Linux runtime cache plus the CPU architecture; a
      # runtime provisioned on Linux is never restored here.
      - name: Cache Hermes runtime
        id: infra-2
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hermes-compat-cache
          key: >-
            hermes-runtime-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('compat/hermes/compatibility-lock.json') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('scripts/provision-hermes-compat') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('scripts/tests/provision-hermes-compat.sh') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('crates/xtask/src/upstream_stage.rs') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/ci.yml') }}

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: hermes-macos
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Install cargo-nextest
        id: infra-3
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@4cef1412cce204788f482e778a0b9187f9626a29 # v2.87.21
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      # Runs the shell tests with /bin/bash (3.2) first on PATH, so the
      # provisioner and the smoke run under the stock macOS shell.
      - name: Check fail-closed Hermes provisioning and smoke scripts
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PATH="/bin:$PATH" /bin/bash scripts/tests/provision-hermes-compat.sh
          PATH="/bin:$PATH" /bin/bash scripts/tests/smoke-hermes-plugin-release.sh

      # Staged and verified as in the Linux job. /bin (bash 3.2) comes first
      # on the PATH the provisioner inherits through `compat stage-upstream`.
      # A cache hit takes about 1.5 minutes (copy, cargo index update, xtask
      # build, verification) and a miss adds the provisioner's bounded
      # downloads; the step timeout turns a hang in either path into a failure
      # within minutes instead of the job timeout.
      - name: Provision locked Hermes runtime
        id: hermes
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cache_dir="${{ runner.temp }}/hermes-compat-cache"
          stage_root="$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-compat"
          stage="$stage_root/hermes"
          rm -rf "$stage_root"
          mkdir -p "$stage_root"
          if [[ -d "$cache_dir" ]]; then
            cp -a "$cache_dir" "$stage"
            cargo xtask compat verify-stage --runtime hermes --dir "$stage_root"
          else
            PATH="/bin:$PATH" cargo xtask compat stage-upstream --runtime hermes --out "$stage_root"
            # A partial cache_dir under an immutable key would poison later
            # runs, so a copy error fails the step; the restored copy is
            # verified on the next hit.
            rm -rf "$cache_dir"
            cp -a "$stage" "$cache_dir"
          fi
          hermes_bin="$stage/venv/bin/hermes"
          printf 'cache=%s\nstage_root=%s\n' "$cache_dir" "$stage_root" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          [[ -f "$hermes_bin" && -x "$hermes_bin" ]] \
            || { echo "provisioned Hermes executable missing at $hermes_bin" >&2; exit 1; }
          printf 'bin=%s\n' "$hermes_bin" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The pinned venv interpreter carries PyYAML; the package tests'
          # plugin harness needs it, and runner Pythons lack it or are
          # group-writable framework builds the harness refuses.
          printf 'python=%s\n' "${hermes_bin%/*}/python" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Every xtask lib test whose name contains `hermes`, one process each.
      # Each run keeps its JUnit report under its own name, because both runs
      # of this job write the macos profile's single report path; that path is
      # cleared first, so a run that writes no report copies none.
      - name: Test Hermes harness natively
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit"
          rm -f target/nextest/macos/junit.xml || exit 1
          cargo nextest run --locked --profile macos -p xtask --lib -E 'test(hermes)'
          status=$?
          cp target/nextest/macos/junit.xml "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit/harness.xml" || status=1
          exit "$status"

      - name: Build offline documentation
        run: cargo xtask docs site

      # The version-A binaries come from `macos-release-build`; this job does
      # not compile them.
      - name: Download the daemon binaries
        id: infra-4
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: macos-release-daemon
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-release-daemon-download

      - name: Unpack the daemon binaries
        id: binaries
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bindir="$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-release-daemon"
          rm -rf "$bindir"
          mkdir -p "$bindir"
          tar -C "$bindir" -xf "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-release-daemon-download/macos-release-daemon.tar"
          for binary in pohunek pohunekd pohunek-sessiond; do
            test -x "$bindir/$binary"
          done
          echo "bindir=$bindir" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # The archive is packaged with the release scripts and extracted outside
      # the checkout, so the gate and the smoke can only use what the published
      # macOS daemon archive contains: the binaries and the packaged smoke
      # script.
      - name: Package and extract the daemon archive outside the source tree
        id: packaged
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="$(awk -F'"' '/^\[workspace\.package\]/ { in_pkg = 1; next } /^\[/ { in_pkg = 0 } in_pkg && /^version[[:space:]]*=/ { print $2; exit }' Cargo.toml)"
          bindir="${{ steps.binaries.outputs.bindir }}"
          dist="$RUNNER_TEMP/dist-daemon"
          rm -rf "$dist"
          mkdir -p "$dist"
          archive="$(packaging/macos/package --development daemon "$version" "$bindir" target/pohunek-docs "$dist")"
          extract_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/packaged-pohunek"
          rm -rf "$extract_dir"
          mkdir -p "$extract_dir"
          tar -xzf "$archive" -C "$extract_dir"
          packaged_dir="$(cd "$extract_dir/$(basename "$archive" .tar.gz)" && pwd -P)"
          if git -C "$packaged_dir" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "packaged directory is inside a Git worktree: $packaged_dir" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          for binary in pohunek pohunekd pohunek-sessiond; do
            test -x "$packaged_dir/$binary"
          done
          test -x "$packaged_dir/packaging/smoke-hermes-plugin-release"
          printf 'dir=%s\n' "$packaged_dir" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # The gate and the smoke install the operator plugin from the Hermes
      # runtime package, built here from runtime-packages/hermes. The smoke's
      # catalog is signed with a throwaway key that only its anchor trusts.
      - name: Build the Hermes runtime package and its throwaway catalog
        id: package
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          package_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-package"
          rm -rf "$package_dir"
          mkdir -p "$package_dir"
          scripts/build-hermes-package "$package_dir/hermes.tar.zst"
          cargo xtask hermes throwaway-catalog \
            --package "$package_dir/hermes.tar.zst" \
            --output-dir "$package_dir/trust"
          printf 'dir=%s\n' "$package_dir" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check pinned Hermes compatibility
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo xtask hermes compatibility \
            --hermes-bin "${{ steps.hermes.outputs.bin }}" \
            --bin-dir "${{ steps.packaged.outputs.dir }}" \
            --package "${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/hermes.tar.zst"

      # The previous step wrote into the stage it used; the next one runs on
      # a fresh restore of the untouched copy at the same absolute path.
      - name: Restore the pristine Hermes stage
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        env:
          CACHE_DIR: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.cache }}
          STAGE_ROOT: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.stage_root }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rm -rf "$STAGE_ROOT/hermes"
          cp -a "$CACHE_DIR" "$STAGE_ROOT/hermes"
          cargo xtask compat verify-stage --runtime hermes --dir "$STAGE_ROOT"

      - name: Smoke packaged plugin installation against pinned Hermes
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          "${{ steps.packaged.outputs.dir }}/packaging/smoke-hermes-plugin-release" \
            "${{ steps.packaged.outputs.dir }}" \
            "${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/hermes.tar.zst" \
            "${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/trust/runtime-catalog.json" \
            "${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/trust/runtime-catalog-anchor.json" \
            "${{ steps.hermes.outputs.bin }}"

      # The CLI-only host route: a sealed copy of the archive that carries the
      # package, its throwaway catalog and the anchor that trusts it, installed
      # with no daemon running.
      - name: Smoke packaged plugin installation without a daemon
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          packaged_dir="${{ steps.packaged.outputs.dir }}"
          trust_dir="${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/trust"
          sealed="$RUNNER_TEMP/packaged-pohunek-sealed"
          rm -rf "$sealed"
          cp -R "$packaged_dir" "$sealed"
          mkdir -p "$sealed/runtime/packages"
          cp "${{ steps.package.outputs.dir }}/hermes.tar.zst" "$sealed/runtime/packages/hermes.tar.zst"
          cp "$trust_dir/runtime-catalog.json" "$sealed/runtime/runtime-catalog.json"
          cp "$trust_dir/runtime-catalog-anchor.json" "$sealed/runtime-catalog-anchor.json"
          chmod 0644 "$sealed/runtime/packages/hermes.tar.zst" "$sealed/runtime/runtime-catalog.json" "$sealed/runtime-catalog-anchor.json"
          component="$(awk '$1 == "component" { print $2 }' "$sealed/MANIFEST")"
          version="$(awk '$1 == "version" { print $2 }' "$sealed/MANIFEST")"
          target="$(awk '$1 == "target" { print $2 }' "$sealed/MANIFEST")"
          signing="$(awk '$1 == "signing" { print $2 }' "$sealed/MANIFEST")"
          minimum="$(awk '$1 == "minimum-macos" { print $2 }' "$sealed/MANIFEST")"
          sh packaging/write-manifest "$sealed" "$component" "$version" "$target" "$signing" $minimum
          "$sealed/packaging/smoke-hermes-plugin-release" --no-daemon "$sealed" \
            "${{ steps.hermes.outputs.bin }}"

      # The test daemon spawns the session worker found beside the test
      # profile, and the release-install scenarios stage the daemon and the
      # worker as a sealed archive, so both are built from this checkout.
      - name: Build the session worker and the daemon
        run: cargo build --locked -p pohunek-session-worker --bin pohunek-sessiond -p pohunek-daemon --bin pohunekd

      # The previous step wrote into the stage it used; the next one runs on
      # a fresh restore of the untouched copy at the same absolute path.
      - name: Restore the pristine Hermes stage
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        env:
          CACHE_DIR: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.cache }}
          STAGE_ROOT: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.stage_root }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rm -rf "$STAGE_ROOT/hermes"
          cp -a "$CACHE_DIR" "$STAGE_ROOT/hermes"
          cargo xtask compat verify-stage --runtime hermes --dir "$STAGE_ROOT"

      # One real pinned Hermes turn through the selected package and the public
      # session commands against a loopback model, natively on arm64. Only the
      # test receives the provisioned executable path; PATH stays the runner's.
      - name: Drive a real pinned Hermes session through the package
        env:
          POHUNEK_HERMES_E2E: "1"
          POHUNEK_HERMES_BIN: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.bin }}
          POHUNEK_PYTHON_BIN: ${{ steps.hermes.outputs.python }}
        shell: /bin/bash {0}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit"
          rm -f target/nextest/macos/junit.xml || exit 1
          cargo nextest run --locked --profile macos -p pohunek-cli --test all -E 'test(/^hermes_package::/)' --run-ignored all --test-threads 1
          status=$?
          cp target/nextest/macos/junit.xml "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit/package.xml" || status=1
          exit "$status"

      - name: Summarize flaky tests
        if: always()
        run: python3 scripts/junit-flaky-summary --label "hermes macos" "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit/harness.xml" "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-junit/package.xml"

      - name: Upload Hermes macOS test reports
        if: always()
        id: infra-5
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: hermes-macos-junit
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hermes-junit/
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # Persist the staged runtime only after the gate and smoke passed.
      - name: Persist Hermes runtime cache
        if: success()
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hermes-compat-cache
          key: >-
            hermes-runtime-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('compat/hermes/compatibility-lock.json') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('scripts/provision-hermes-compat') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('scripts/tests/provision-hermes-compat.sh') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('crates/xtask/src/upstream_stage.rs') }}-
            ${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/ci.yml') }}
      - name: Cancel the run (fail fast)
        if: failure() && env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE == '' && steps.infra-1.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-2.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-3.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-4.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-5.outcome != 'failure' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        uses: ./.github/actions/cancel-run
      - name: Note the infrastructure failure (no cancel)
        if: failure() && (env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE != '' || steps.infra-1.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-2.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-3.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-4.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-5.outcome == 'failure')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::notice title=Infrastructure failure::tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step); check the step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too; not cancelling, rerun this job alone"

  # Each test runs at most once per OS in a run (#1226): this job reads every
  # JUnit report of the run and fails on a test two jobs of the same OS ran,
  # unless scripts/test-duplicates.json allows it with a reason. It runs in the
  # main and nightly tiers, where every test job runs.
bodies.integration:
name: tests (heavy, PTY + Hermes)
    needs: [build-tests, test-selection, reuse]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-tests.result == 'success' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.test-selection.result != 'success' || needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed != 'true' || needs.test-selection.outputs.heavy != 'false') && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'integration') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: relocated
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        id: infra-1
        with:
          path: relocated
          persist-credentials: false

      # The sparse test tree and the relocated checkout hold no .github/actions
      # at the workspace root when the cancel step runs, so the action is copied
      # out of the checkout next to it.
      - name: Keep the fail-fast action
        run: cp -R .github/actions/cancel-run "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/cancel-run-action"

      - name: Install cargo-nextest
        id: infra-2
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@4cef1412cce204788f482e778a0b9187f9626a29 # v2.87.21
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest

      # xtask::dependency_policy reads `cargo metadata --offline`, so this job
      # needs the locked crates in the cargo registry. It compiles nothing
      # else: the test binaries come from the archive.
      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./relocated/.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Fetch locked dependency sources
        run: |
          # CARGO_NET_RETRY retries spurious failures inside cargo with a
          # per-request CARGO_HTTP_TIMEOUT; the helper retries a hung fetch
          # whose request never returns.
          "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/relocated/.github/scripts/ci-retry" --label cargo-fetch \
            --attempts "$CI_RETRY_ATTEMPTS" \
            --attempt-timeout "$CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_CARGO_SECONDS" \
            --backoff "$CI_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS" -- \
            cargo fetch --locked

      - name: Download test archive
        id: infra-3
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: nextest-archive
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nextest-archive

      # The daemon socket tests spawn the real durable worker by path
      # (`target/debug/pohunek-sessiond`); it comes out of the archive, which
      # cannot be built without it.
      - name: Verify exhaustive disjoint test partitions
        run: python3 scripts/test-partitions --archive-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/nextest-archive/nextest-archive.tar.zst" check

      - name: Download test selection
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true'
        id: infra-4
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-selection
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/test-selection

      # The tests run from a tree holding only the files whose change selects
      # them, so a read of any other path fails instead of passing with the
      # test skipped. A run without sparse.txt keeps the full tree.
      - name: Keep only the selection's files in the tree
        if: env.TEST_SELECTION_SPARSE == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sparse="$RUNNER_TEMP/test-selection/sparse.txt"
          if [ -f "$sparse" ]; then
            git sparse-checkout set --no-cone --stdin < "$sparse"
            echo "sparse tree of $(wc -l < "$sparse") files"
          fi

      - name: Heavy tests (bounded nextest concurrency)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SHARD: heavy
          NARROWED: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.test-selection.result == 'success' && needs.test-selection.outputs.narrowed == 'true' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          selection=()
          if [ "$NARROWED" = true ]; then
            selection=(--selection "$RUNNER_TEMP/test-selection/selection.json")
          fi
          python3 scripts/test-partitions --archive-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/nextest-archive/nextest-archive.tar.zst" run "$SHARD" "${selection[@]}"

      - name: Summarize flaky tests
        if: always()
        run: python3 scripts/junit-flaky-summary --label heavy target/nextest/heavy/junit.xml

      # Per-test timing evidence for the test-performance work (JUnit `time`
      # attributes). Nextest writes the report under its own storage directory.
      - name: Upload integration test report
        if: always()
        id: infra-5
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: nextest-junit-heavy
          path: relocated/target/nextest/heavy/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn
      - name: Cancel the run (fail fast)
        if: failure() && env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE == '' && steps.infra-1.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-2.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-3.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-4.outcome != 'failure' && steps.infra-5.outcome != 'failure' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        uses: ./cancel-run-action
      - name: Note the infrastructure failure (no cancel)
        if: failure() && (env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE != '' || steps.infra-1.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-2.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-3.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-4.outcome == 'failure' || steps.infra-5.outcome == 'failure')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::notice title=Infrastructure failure::tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step); check the step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too; not cancelling, rerun this job alone"

  # Issue #100: the ignored real-systemd suites drive the runner's own systemd
  # user manager (transient worker units, the namespaced daemon unit, the
  # `pohunek service` transactions, and the workflow plugin units of #326). Hosted Ubuntu runners run a user manager
  # without lingering; the bus address is exported because the job shell does
  # not carry one.
bodies.macos-package:
# macOS 15 is the tested platform. The archives target macOS 14.0, a
    # supported build target that CI does not run (issue #1224).
    name: macOS package install and upgrade (macos-15)
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.result == 'success' && needs.macos-release-build.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && (inputs.tier == 'main' || inputs.tier == 'nightly')) || github.event_name == 'push' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.macos_package == 'true')) && !contains(fromJSON(needs.reuse.outputs.skip || '[]'), 'macos-package') }}
    needs: [changes, macos-release-build, reuse]
    runs-on: macos-15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      # mold is Linux-only: keep the default linker on macOS runners.
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Verify native runner architecture
        shell: bash
        run: test "$(uname -m)" = "arm64"

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: macos-package-macos-15
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Build offline documentation
        run: cargo xtask docs site

      # The version-A binaries come from `macos-release-build`; this job does
      # not compile them.
      - name: Download the daemon binaries
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: macos-release-daemon
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-release-daemon-download

      - name: Unpack the daemon binaries
        id: build
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bindir="$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-release-daemon"
          rm -rf "$bindir"
          mkdir -p "$bindir"
          tar -C "$bindir" -xf "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-release-daemon-download/macos-release-daemon.tar"
          for binary in pohunek pohunekd pohunek-sessiond; do
            test -x "$bindir/$binary"
          done
          echo "bindir=$bindir" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Package version A
        id: package-a
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="$(awk -F'"' '/^\[workspace\.package\]/ { in_pkg = 1; next } /^\[/ { in_pkg = 0 } in_pkg && /^version[[:space:]]*=/ { print $2; exit }' Cargo.toml)"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist-a"
          staging="$(packaging/macos/package --stage-release daemon "$version" \
            "${{ steps.build.outputs.bindir }}" target/pohunek-docs "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist-a")"
          archive="$(packaging/macos/package --adhoc-release daemon "$version" "$staging")"
          packaging/macos/verify-signed --adhoc "$staging"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "archive=$archive" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # The same commit rebuilt here from a cold release directory, at the same
      # checkout path as on the builder's runner, must produce the builder's
      # binaries and the same archive. Cargo mixes the RUSTFLAGS text (which
      # carries the checkout path for path remapping) into every crate's
      # metadata hash, so the path itself stays fixed.
      - name: Rebuild from a cold release directory and compare
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.tier == 'nightly') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The builder's job summary names its runner image, for a mismatch.
          echo "Runner image: ${ImageOS:-unknown} ${ImageVersion:-unknown}"
          first="$RUNNER_TEMP/first-binaries"
          mkdir -p "$first" "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist-repro"
          for binary in pohunek pohunekd pohunek-sessiond; do
            cp "${{ steps.build.outputs.bindir }}/$binary" "$first/"
          done
          rm -rf target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release
          bindir="$(packaging/macos/build-release daemon)"
          for binary in pohunek pohunekd pohunek-sessiond; do
            cmp "$first/$binary" "$bindir/$binary" \
              || { echo "::error::$binary is not reproducible from a cold build"; exit 1; }
          done
          rebuilt_staging="$(packaging/macos/package --stage-release daemon \
            "${{ steps.package-a.outputs.version }}" "$bindir" target/pohunek-docs "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist-repro")"
          rebuilt="$(packaging/macos/package --adhoc-release daemon \
            "${{ steps.package-a.outputs.version }}" "$rebuilt_staging")"
          cmp "${{ steps.package-a.outputs.archive }}" "$rebuilt" \
            || { echo "::error::the daemon archive is not reproducible from a cold build"; exit 1; }

      # A second version of the same tree, so the upgrade installs different
      # real binaries. The workspace version is bumped only in this runner's
      # checkout and restored afterwards.
      - name: Build and package version B
        id: package-b
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version_b="$(python3 - <<'PY'
          import re
          text = open("Cargo.toml").read()

name: Upgrade test

# A session started on the previous release's published binaries must survive
# `pohunek service upgrade` to this build (issue #525). The job installs the
# previous release from its GitHub Release assets (checksum verified, never
# rebuilt), starts a session on that release's built-in Claude and Codex
# runtimes with a fake agent that runs the managed hooks, upgrades through the
# operator path, and asserts the preflight judges the session adoptable, the
# session stays live and its screen and input work, the hooks of the adopted
# worker are refused until the session relaunches when the previous release
# speaks protocol 4 (from 0.41.0 on they are admitted), stop/resume relaunch
# from the same package digest with the native reference and their hooks report
# turn errors, and the previous release's own CLI is refused with a version
# mismatch when it speaks protocol 4 (from 0.41.0 on it reads and writes
# through its own client, the window being protocol 5 only). The upgrade
# installs the official runtime packages from the head build's `runtime/` tree
# (written by `cargo xtask release test-runtime`). scripts/upgrade-test does the
# work; crates/cli/tests/release_upgrade.rs holds the assertions.
#
# Callers:
# - ci.yml runs it on pull requests that touch the daemon, worker, protocol or
#   CLI crates, and on push to main, the weekly schedule and manual CI runs;
# - release.yml runs it on a release tag, before any binary is built for
#   publishing, with the tagged commit as the target and the newest earlier
#   release as the previous one;
# - `gh workflow run upgrade.yml -f previous_tag=v0.34.2 -f head_ref=<ref>`
#   runs it on any pair. The harness (script and test) always comes from the
#   ref the workflow is dispatched on; `head_ref` selects only the source built
#   as the upgrade target, so an older tree without the harness can be tested.
#   `head_ref` is a branch, tag or commit of this repository, never a fork
#   head (`refs/pull/<N>/head` or a fork commit).

# Linux jobs stay on ubuntu-24.04 (#1731), never ubuntu-latest: they build, assemble or run the shipped binaries, and the
# acceptance guests carry glibc 2.41, which `glibc-check` enforces; ubuntu-26.04 has glibc 2.43.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      previous_tag:
        description: Release tag to install first (vX.Y.Z), or `latest` for the newest published release
        type: string
        default: latest
      head_ref:
        description: Branch, tag or commit of this repository (never a fork head) built as the upgrade target; empty means the ref this run was started on
        type: string
        default: ''
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      previous_tag:
        description: Release tag to install first (vX.Y.Z), or `latest` for the newest published release
        type: string
        default: latest
      head_ref:
        description: Branch, tag or commit of this repository (never a fork head) built as the upgrade target; empty means the caller's ref
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  # Pinned mold release; the same pin as ci.yml (MOLD_SHA256 is the sha256
  # GitHub publishes for mold-2.42.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz). Bump both together,
  # and in gate-tests.yml, release.yml and release-build.yml.
  MOLD_VERSION: "2.42.1"
  MOLD_SHA256: 6ff270c9bf07d2bec5c98aa324eb7c4daf6a1a4d815c05ff1708049616047855

    name: upgrade from the previous release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PREVIOUS_TAG: ${{ inputs.previous_tag }}
      HEAD_REF: ${{ inputs.head_ref }}
    steps:
      # The harness: scripts/upgrade-test and the release_upgrade test.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The upgrade target, when it is not the harness's own tree.
      - name: Check out the upgrade target
        if: ${{ inputs.head_ref != '' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.head_ref }}
          path: head-src

      - name: Install mold linker
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-mold
        timeout-minutes: 10
        with:
          version: ${{ env.MOLD_VERSION }}
          sha256: ${{ env.MOLD_SHA256 }}

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-rust

      - name: Cache cargo build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          # The same compile cache as the other debug jobs; this job only
          # restores it.
          shared-key: bins

      # archive cache can be keyed by it. When the target is a release tag
      # (a tag push, or a tag named by head_ref), that tag is never the
      # previous release.
      - name: Resolve the previous release
        id: previous
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          exclude=""
          if [[ "$HEAD_REF" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then

          echo "Previous release: $tag (target: ${HEAD_REF:-$GITHUB_REF})"

      # release on every run, so the cache is never trusted.
      - name: Cache the previous release archive

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upgrade-archives
          key: upgrade-archives-${{ steps.previous.outputs.tag }}

      # against its own systemd user manager, like `systemd-supervision`
      # (scripts/upgrade-test --current-user refuses to run anywhere else).
      - name: Require a running systemd user manager

          systemctl --version | head -n 1
          echo "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/bus" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          systemctl --user is-system-running --wait || systemctl --user is-system-running | grep -qx degraded

      - name: Upgrade test
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          head_dir="."
          if [ -n "$HEAD_REF" ]; then head_dir="head-src"; fi
          scripts/upgrade-test \
            --previous "${{ steps.previous.outputs.tag }}" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --head-dir "$head_dir" \
            --cache-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/upgrade-archives" \
            --artifacts-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/upgrade-goldens" \
            --current-user

      # The previous release's store and protocol goldens, for the
      # fixture-based tests, kept even when the upgrade fails.
      - name: Upload the previous release's goldens
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: upgrade-goldens-${{ steps.previous.outputs.tag }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upgrade-goldens
          if-no-files-found: warn

preamble:
name: CI

# Test everything on every push to main and on every pull request: formatting,
# lints (warnings are errors), the full test suite, and a release build of both
# binaries so a broken release profile is caught before tagging. Doctests run on
# every pull request. The release build (job `release-build`) runs on push to
# main, the daily schedule, and manual dispatch, and on pull requests only when
# the `release` paths filter matches (manifests, lockfile, .cargo, toolchain
# pins, the release/CI workflows, scripts/release, packaging). The release
# rehearsal (jobs `release-rehearsal-build`, `release-rehearsal-scenarios` and
# `release-rehearsal`) runs the reusable release workflows with a throwaway key
# and publishes nothing; it is part of the nightly tier, not of the main tier.
# The rehearsal's synthetic-archive smoke scenarios (#1259) are their own job
# that needs only this checkout, so they start in parallel with the build.
# Runner images are pinned (#1731), never ubuntu-latest. The nextest archive producer (build-tests) and every job
# that consumes its archive run on ubuntu-26.04, together, so they share one glibc. Jobs that build or run the
# shipped binaries stay on ubuntu-24.04: the acceptance guests carry glibc 2.41 and `glibc-check` rejects binaries
# built against 26.04's glibc 2.43. The other jobs stay on ubuntu-24.04 until a run on 26.04 covers them.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tier:
        description: CI tier to run
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - main
          - nightly
      dispatch_id:
        description: Correlates an automated evidence request with its workflow run
        required: false
        type: string
      delta:
        description: Reuse the green jobs of the pull request run of the same tree (opt-in; scripts/release dispatches stay full)
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean
  # Daily sweep to catch regressions in jobs that are path-filtered out on
  # normal PRs (issue #125). Runs at 05:00 UTC; `pull_request_target`
  # is intentionally avoided to keep the default pull-request provenance model.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 5 * * *'

run-name: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('CI [tier={0}]{1}{2}', inputs.tier, inputs.dispatch_id != '' && format(' [dispatch={0}]', inputs.dispatch_id) || '', inputs.delta && ' [delta]' || '') || ' ' }}


# A cancelling-set job that fails deterministically in a pull request or
# `workflow_dispatch` run cancels the run (#1075): the job's
# `Cancel the run (fail fast)` step uses .github/actions/cancel-run. The
# cancelling set is the jobs in the `test-selection-verdict` `needs:` list
# minus the advisory `audit` and the fail-open `test-selection` and `reuse`
# decisions, plus the two jobs that also carry the step outside the verdict
# set (`package-version-bump`, `docs`); every other job never cancels, and
# a called workflow never cancels either: its failure shows as `failure` on
# the run page. The step needs `actions: write`, granted per job and never
# for the workflow. Push runs, scheduled runs, the advisory audit job and a
# job that was itself cancelled never trigger it. The failing job and the
# run end as `cancelled`, so no job shows `failure` on the run page; the
# `::error` annotation on the failed job's check run (and its job summary)
# names the job's display name, job id, link and failed step.
# Infrastructure marking (#2205) is deterministic: `env.CI_INFRA_FAILURE` (set
# by .github/scripts/ci-retry when its retries are exhausted) or a failed
# network `uses:` step tagged with an `infra-` id (taiki-e/install-action,
# actions/download-artifact and upload-artifact, actions/setup-node,
# actions/cache restore, oven-sh/setup-bun, actions/checkout). A failure
# tagged as infrastructure (an exhausted retry or a failed network step)
# never runs the cancel step; instead the `Note the infrastructure failure
# (no cancel)` step writes a `::notice` and the run continues. Check the
# step log: a deterministic failure of a retried command is tagged too,
# so rerunning the failed job alone recovers only from a flaky download.
# A new PR push cancels the PR's run in progress (latest wins). Pushes to main
# drain (#1209): the running main run completes, and GitHub keeps only the
# newest push pending behind it, replacing an older pending one. Each scheduled
# or manual run gets its own group, so it neither cancels nor waits for those.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'pr' || github.event_name == 'push' && 'main' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings
  # Disable incremental compilation in CI: rust-cache strips incremental
  # artifacts before persisting anyway, so producing them only wastes time.
  # Kept explicit (issue #124) so every job benefits even before restore.
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  # G2 of #1218: a narrowed pull request runs its tests from a sparse tree
  # holding only the files whose change selects them. Off until three
  # consecutive nightly G3 runs on main pass, plus the local preflight.
  TEST_SELECTION_SPARSE: "false"
  # A Python script never imports from its own directory or the working
  # directory, so a file a pull request adds there cannot shadow a module.
  PYTHONSAFEPATH: "1"
  # Test binaries (issue #170): job `build-tests` compiles the workspace test
  # binaries once (`cargo nextest archive --workspace --all-features`) and
  # uploads the archive. The test jobs (fast shards, heavy) download
  # it and run from it via scripts/test-partitions --archive-file; they install
  # only cargo-nextest, no rust-cache (the heavy job also needs the fetched
  # crate sources for xtask::dependency_policy). Tests
  # resolve binaries and sources at run time (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`,
  # `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, the worker beside the test binaries), so the archive
  # is relocatable: the test jobs check the repository out into `relocated/`,
  # a different absolute path than the one `build-tests` compiled at, and every
  # run proves it. `.config/nextest.toml` archive.include makes the archive
  # build fail when pohunek-sessiond is missing, so a test never runs without
  # its worker.
  # Job `build-bins` stays a separate default-feature build: the archive
  # compiles with --all-features, which enables cli's `test-util` seams, and
  # the SDK e2e job must exercise shipped binaries. The Hermes jobs build their
  # binaries with default features in-job for the same reason.
  # Compile cache (issue #164): Swatinem/rust-cache is the only compile-cache
  # layer. Each Rust job restores the entry of its job type (`shared-key`:
  # clippy, test-debug, bins, systemd, release, xtask, docs, hack, nightly-udeps,
  # platform-contracts, darwin-check). The key does not name the runner image, so
  # a cache is never restored on an older image than the one that saved it: a
  # cache built on ubuntu-26.04 must not feed an ubuntu-24.04 job. The full key
  # also hashes the toolchain, the
  # RUST*/CARGO* environment (RUSTFLAGS included), and the Cargo manifests.
  # rust-cache saves only on a key miss and the first finisher wins, so each
  # key has exactly one designated saver, the job that builds the superset
  # of the key's artifacts; every other job in the group sets `save-if:
  # false`. The saver saves only for refs/heads/main (push, schedule, and
  # dispatch on main): PR runs restore main's entries and never evict them.
  # The mold -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold RUSTFLAGS live in each Linux Rust
  # job's `env`, not here, because the macOS and docs jobs do not install
  # mold. .github/actions/setup-mold puts mold on PATH without touching
  # /usr/bin/ld: only those RUSTFLAGS select mold.
  # Pinned mold release for .github/actions/setup-mold. MOLD_SHA256 is the
  # sha256 GitHub publishes for the release asset
  # mold-2.42.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz (`gh api repos/rui314/mold/releases/tags/v2.42.1`,
  # asset `digest`), cross-checked against a local download. Bump both together, and in
  # upgrade.yml, gate-tests.yml, release.yml and release-build.yml.
  MOLD_VERSION: "2.42.1"
  MOLD_SHA256: 6ff270c9bf07d2bec5c98aa324eb7c4daf6a1a4d815c05ff1708049616047855
  # Pinned zig release for .github/actions/setup-zig, used only as the C compiler
  # of the `darwin-check` job. ZIG_SHA256 is the sha256 ziglang.org publishes for
  # zig-x86_64-linux-0.17.0.tar.xz (https://ziglang.org/download/index.json).
  # Bump both together.
  ZIG_VERSION: "0.17.0"
  ZIG_SHA256: 1cbe9df9f27e6b78d14ccbca43b6703a404ef79ef1c463de901d7f088d4e2026
  # Time limit of the release baseline download in `package-selection`. The
  # assets it selects are small (release v0.34.2: 10 files, 15 KB in all), so
  # a healthy download is one API listing plus a request per file, done in
  # seconds; two minutes leaves room for slow requests and larger packages. A
  # download that runs out of time counts as failed: every package job runs.
  PACKAGE_BASELINE_FETCH_TIMEOUT: 120s
  # Retry bounds for `.github/scripts/ci-retry`, shared by every network
  # install that runs through it (apt-get, npm ci, bun install, rustup, uv,
  # cargo fetch; issue #2201). Three attempts with a 10 s backoff bound every
  # class: each attempt carries its own connect/total timeout (apt 30/180 s,
  # the rest 180 s), so a hung mirror fails an attempt instead of the step.
  # The worst case (3 x (180 s + KILL_GRACE_SECONDS) + 10 s + 20 s backoff)
  # fits the smallest 10-minute step limit with headroom.
  # Attempt timeouts come from the one calibrated set of CI_RETRY_* values
  # in this workflow's top-level env (p90 of 29 successful main runs plus
  # headroom, per command class: cargo fetch 7 s, apt/oomd 17 s, bun 3 s,
  # rustup 13 s, uv 8 s, zig 16 s; `scripts/ci-timings steps --limit 30`)
  # and from the matching action/retry knobs named in each comment below:
  # - apt: Acquire::http(s)::Timeout=30 already on every call (apt docs:
  #   `man apt.conf`, the `Acquire::http::Timeout` option); the helper
  #   bounds the total.
  # - npm: the tool defaults stay in force (npm docs:
  #   https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/config#fetch-timeout and
  #   #fetch-retries: --fetch-timeout=300000, --fetch-retries=2). npm's own
  #   retries run inside one install; the helper bounds the total install
  #   time and retries the whole install after npm's retries are exhausted.
  # - bun: the tool default stays in force (BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_COUNT=5,
  #   bun docs: https://bun.sh/docs/installation#configuring-bun; bun has
  #   no timeout knob). One timed-out request already ends the attempt,
  #   so the helper retries the whole install instead.
  # - rustup: RUSTUP_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT bounds each download from inside and
  #   RUSTUP_MAX_RETRIES retries it (rustup docs:
  #   https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/devel/environment-variables.html);
  #   RUSTUP_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT equals the helper attempt timeout, so the
  #   helper always fires first and bounds a hung install whose request
  #   never returns.
  # - uv: the tool defaults stay in force (uv docs:
  #   https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#http-timeout:
  #   UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT/UV_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, UV_HTTP_RETRIES); the
  #   helper retries a hung download whose request never returns.
  # - cargo: the tool defaults stay in force (cargo docs:
  #   https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#netretry:
  #   CARGO_NET_RETRY, CARGO_HTTP_TIMEOUT). CARGO_NET_RETRY retries
  #   spurious failures inside cargo and CARGO_HTTP_TIMEOUT bounds each
  #   request; the helper retries a hung fetch whose request never
  #   returns.
  # - setup-zig: curl --connect-timeout/--max-time (mold parity, plus a
  #   stall --speed-limit/--speed-time since curl retries only attempts that
  #   return, curl docs: https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html) bound each
  #   download; the helper is not wrapped around curl because a curl
  #   transfer is already one bounded attempt.
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPTS: "3"
  CI_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS: "10"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_APT_SECONDS: "180"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_NPM_SECONDS: "180"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_BUN_SECONDS: "180"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_RUSTUP_SECONDS: "180"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_UV_SECONDS: "180"
  CI_RETRY_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_CARGO_SECONDS: "180"
  # Releases listed by `package-version-bump` to find the last released
  # version at or below the workspace version. `gh release list` returns the
  # newest releases first, and the wanted release is the newest one at or
  # below the workspace version; 200 is far more releases than are published
  # between two workspace version bumps.
  PACKAGE_BUMP_RELEASE_LIMIT: 200
